Used exclusively in the direct-add flow: when the provided email matches an existing active erp_hrm_members account, this roleId is validated to confirm it references an existing erp_hrm_roles record with erp_hrm_organization_id = organizationId, then used to set role_id on the newly inserted erp_hrm_organization_members record. Validation: must be a valid UUID referencing erp_hrm_roles.id scoped to the target organization; reject with 422 if not found.

employmentType.description: The employment classification for the invitee within the organization. Allowed values are: `full-time`, `part-time`, `contractor`, or `intern`. This classification is applied when the invitee is added as an organization member.
employmentType.x-autobe-specification: Not stored on erp_hrm_invitations. Used exclusively in the direct-add flow: when the provided email matches an existing active erp_hrm_members account, this value is used to set employment_type on the newly inserted erp_hrm_organization_members record. Allowed values: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', 'intern'. Reject with 422 if an invalid value is provided.

IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate.description:
Request body for issuing a new invitation to bring a prospective employee into an organization.

Provide the email address of the person to invite, the role they should be assigned within the organization, and their employment classification. The organization context is established by the path parameter, and the issuing member's identity is resolved automatically from the authenticated session.

If the invited email already belongs to an active platform account, the system will immediately add that person to the organization and mark the invitation as accepted. Otherwise, the invitation will remain pending until the person registers using the invited email address.
IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This is the request body DTO for POST /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/invitations. It collects the minimum information needed to create an invitation record: the target email address and the onboarding parameters (role and employment type) that are applied if/when the invitee is added as an organization member. The erp_hrm_organization_id is resolved from the path parameter organizationId. The erp_hrm_organization_member_id (issuing member identity) is resolved from the authenticated JWT session. erp_hrm_member_id is server-resolved by looking up erp_hrm_members.email. status defaults to 'pending' (or 'accepted' in the direct-add flow). id, created_at, updated_at are auto-generated. roleId and employmentType are not stored on erp_hrm_invitations but are applied to the erp_hrm_organization_members record created during the direct-add flow.

status.x-autobe-specification: When non-null, apply WHERE erp_hrm_projects.status = :status. The value must match one of the allowed erp_hrm_projects.status values: 'active' (work ongoing), 'archived' (suspended/on hold), 'completed' (work finished). Return 400 Bad Request for any unrecognized value. When null or omitted, no status filter is applied and projects of all statuses are returned (excluding soft-deleted records).

Default: 'created_at' when null or omitted. Used in conjunction with the 'order' field.

order.x-autobe-specification: Controls the ORDER BY direction in the SQL query. Allowed values: 'asc' → ASC, 'desc' → DESC. Default: 'desc' when null or omitted. Applied together with the 'sort' field.

page.x-autobe-specification: 1-indexed page number for pagination. Used to compute OFFSET = (:page - 1) * :limit. Must be >= 1. Defaults to 1 when omitted. Controls which page of results is returned.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of projects to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 when not specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records to return per page. Used as the LIMIT value in the SQL query. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Controls page size.

IErpHrmProject.IRequest.description:
Request body for retrieving a paginated and filtered list of projects within the authenticated member's current organization.

All fields are optional. When omitted, all non-deleted projects in the organization are returned using default pagination settings. The organization scope is automatically determined from the authenticated member's session context — no organization identifier needs to be provided in the request body.

Supports filtering by project lifecycle status and free-text search on project name. Pagination is controlled by page number and items-per-page limit. Results can be sorted by project name, creation date, status, budget hours, or planned dates.
IErpHrmProject.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is the request body for the PATCH /erpHrm/member/projects endpoint. It carries optional filter and pagination parameters for querying the erp_hrm_projects table. Implementation steps: (1) Resolve organization_id from the authenticated member's JWT session — it is NOT a field in this DTO. (2) Apply WHERE erp_hrm_projects.organization_id = <session_org_id> AND deleted_at IS NULL. (3) If 'status' is provided (non-null), add AND erp_hrm_projects.status = :status (must be one of: 'active', 'archived', 'completed'; return 400 for unrecognized values). (4) If 'search' is provided, apply AND erp_hrm_projects.name ILIKE '%:search%' leveraging the GIN trigram index on name. (5) Apply ORDER BY <sort> <order>, defaulting to created_at DESC. (6) Apply LIMIT :limit OFFSET (:page - 1) * :limit with defaults: page=1, limit=20. (7) Return IPageIErpHrmProject.ISummary with paginated data and total count metadata.

status.x-autobe-specification: Filter applied as: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.status IN (...status). Allowed values per DB schema: 'pending', 'accepted', 'rejected', 'expired', 'cancelled'. If omitted or empty, no status filter is applied and invitations of all statuses are returned.

IErpHrmInvitation.IRequest.description:
Request body for retrieving a paginated and filtered list of invitations within a specific organization.

All fields are optional. When omitted, no filtering is applied for that criterion and default pagination values are used. Multiple status values can be supplied to match invitations in any of those states (e.g., retrieve all pending invitations by passing `["pending"]`).

The `email` field supports partial matching, making it easy to search for invitations sent to a specific domain or address pattern. Date range filters (`createdAtFrom`, `createdAtTo`) allow narrowing results to a specific time window. The `invitingMemberId` filter isolates invitations issued by a particular organization member.
IErpHrmInvitation.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This is a filter and pagination request DTO for querying erp_hrm_invitations scoped to a specific organization. The organizationId is sourced from the URL path parameter and must not appear here. The authenticated member identity is resolved from the JWT token. Implementation steps: (1) Apply status filter: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.status IN (...status) if provided, else no status filter. (2) Apply email filter: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.email ILIKE '%email%' using the GIN trigram index on erp_hrm_invitations.email. (3) Apply invitingMemberId filter: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.erp_hrm_organization_member_id = invitingMemberId. (4) Apply date range: WHERE erp_hrm_invitations.created_at >= createdAtFrom AND/OR <= createdAtTo. (5) Pagination: offset = (page - 1) * limit, default page=1, default limit=20, max limit=100. (6) Sorting: ORDER BY erp_hrm_invitations.created_at ASC for 'createdAt_asc', DESC for 'createdAt_desc'; default DESC. Use the composite index (erp_hrm_organization_id, status, created_at) for efficient filtering.

status.description: The new status to apply to the invitation. Only `pending` invitations may be updated. Valid target values are: `cancelled` (revoked by an administrator), `rejected` (declined by the invitee or an administrator), or `expired` (explicitly marked as lapsed). Attempting any other transition returns a 422 error.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to `erp_hrm_invitations.status`. The service layer must enforce: (1) current `status` must be `pending`; (2) new `status` must be one of `cancelled`, `rejected`, or `expired`. The value `accepted` is never valid through this endpoint. On success, persist the new status and update `updated_at` to NOW().

IErpHrmInvitation.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating an existing invitation within an organization. Used exclusively to transition the `status` of a `pending` invitation to one of `cancelled`, `rejected`, or `expired`. All other invitation fields are immutable and managed by the system.
IErpHrmInvitation.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Maps exclusively to the `erp_hrm_invitations.status` column. This DTO is the request body for `PUT /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/invitations/{invitationId}`. On receipt, the service layer must: (1) verify the authenticated member belongs to the target organization with Owner/Manager permission, (2) fetch the invitation by `id = invitationId` AND `erp_hrm_organization_id = organizationId`, (3) assert the current `status` is `pending` — if not, return 422, (4) assert the requested `status` is one of `cancelled`, `rejected`, or `expired` — if not, return 422, (5) set `status` to the new value and `updated_at` to the current timestamp. The `accepted` transition is never permitted through this endpoint; it is handled internally by the sign-up flow.

Must reference an existing, non-deleted erp_hrm_organization_members record that belongs to the same organization as the target project. The member must have an 'active' status; deactivated members cannot be newly assigned to projects.

projectRole.description: The project-scoped role to assign to the member. Must be either `member` (standard contributor who can log time and view tasks) or `project-lead` (manager-level role that also grants task creation, editing, and status management authority within the project).
projectRole.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_project_members.project_role. Must be exactly 'member' or 'project-lead'. Any other value is rejected. 'member' grants standard contributor access (time logging, task viewing). 'project-lead' additionally grants task creation, editing, and status management authority within the project.

IErpHrmProjectMember.ICreate.description: Request body for assigning an organization member to a specific project, creating a new project membership record. The target project is identified by the `projectId` path parameter. The caller must provide the UUID of the organization member to assign and the project-scoped role they will hold. Allowed project roles are `member` (a standard contributor who can log time against the project and view its tasks) and `project-lead` (a manager-level role that additionally grants task creation, editing, and status management authority within the project). The target organization member must be active, belong to the same organization as the project, and must not already be assigned to the project.
IErpHrmProjectMember.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This Create DTO maps directly to an INSERT operation on erp_hrm_project_members. The organization_member_id column is populated from organizationMemberId in the request body. The project_role column is populated from projectRole. The project_id column is derived from the {projectId} path parameter, not from this body. The id is a newly generated UUID. created_at and updated_at are set to the current server timestamp. deleted_at is initialized to null. Validation requirements: (1) organizationMemberId must reference an existing, non-deleted erp_hrm_organization_members record belonging to the same organization as the target project; (2) projectRole must be exactly 'member' or 'project-lead'; (3) a unique constraint check on (organization_member_id, project_id) must pass — if a non-deleted record already exists, return 409 Conflict. The caller must hold the project:manage permission in their organization role.

IErpHrmEmployeeContract.description:
Represents a formal employment contract record for an organization member within the ERP HRM system.

Each contract captures the agreed-upon employment terms at a specific point in time: the monetary compensation amount per pay period (`payRate`), the payment frequency (`payPeriod`), the contracted working hours per week (`workingHoursPerWeek`), the effective start date (`startDate`), an optional end date (`endDate`), and optional supplementary notes.

Contracts are immutable once created. When employment terms change, the active contract is deactivated and a new contract record is created, preserving the full history. The `isActive` flag indicates whether this contract is the currently effective employment agreement for the member. At most one contract per organization member may be active at a time.

Valid values for `payPeriod` are: `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `bi_weekly`, `monthly`, `annually`.
IErpHrmEmployeeContract.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the erp_hrm_employee_contracts table. All scalar columns are mapped 1:1 to camelCase DTO properties. The FK column organization_member_id is exposed as the scalar UUID field organizationMemberId (not expanded to a nested object), consistent with the operation specification which treats the organizationMemberId as a path parameter and response field. The organizationMember belongs-to relation is excluded from the DTO. pay_period stores one of: 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'bi_weekly', 'monthly', 'annually'. end_date and notes are nullable (oneOf with null). is_active indicates the currently effective contract; at most one contract per member may be active. Contracts are immutable after creation — updated_at changes only when is_active is toggled.

project_role.description: The new project-scoped role to assign to the membership. Use `member` to grant standard contributor access (time logging, task visibility) or `project-lead` to grant project manager authority (includes creating, editing, and managing tasks within this project). This is the only attribute of a project membership that can be changed after creation.
project_role.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_project_members.project_role. Accepted values are exactly 'member' or 'project-lead', enforced by the regex pattern `^(member|project-lead)$`. On PUT, write this value to the project_role column and set updated_at = NOW(). If the submitted value matches the existing value, the update is still processed (no-op result) and the record is returned unchanged.

IErpHrmProjectMember.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating the project-scoped role of an existing project membership. The only mutable attribute of a project membership is the `project_role`, which controls the member's authority level within the project. Supply the desired role value — either `member` for a standard contributor or `project-lead` for a project manager with task management authority. All other membership attributes (the assigned member, parent project, and timestamps) are immutable and are supplied via path parameters or managed by the system.
IErpHrmProjectMember.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to the erp_hrm_project_members table for the PUT /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/members/{projectMemberId} endpoint. This DTO accepts a single mutable field: project_role. Implementation steps: (1) Validate that project_role is one of the allowed string values: 'member' or 'project-lead'. The pattern constraint `^(member|project-lead)$` enforces this. (2) Perform the UPDATE on erp_hrm_project_members setting project_role = requestBody.project_role and updated_at = NOW() where id = projectMemberId AND project_id = projectId AND deleted_at IS NULL. (3) If the new role is identical to the existing role, proceed with no-op update and return 200 with the current record. Path parameters projectId and projectMemberId are used for record lookup, not present in this DTO. The actor's organization_member_id and created_at are system-managed and excluded.

IErpHrmDepartment.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing department within an organization.

Allows authorized members (those holding the `org:manage` permission) to modify a department's identifying and structural attributes. The mutable fields are the department's display name, its optional description, and its optional parent department reference that controls placement in the two-tier organizational hierarchy.

The department's name must remain unique within the organization after the update. If a parent department is specified, it must be a top-level department in the same organization (cannot itself have a parent). A department that already has child departments cannot be given a parent, as this would violate the one-level nesting constraint. Setting `parentId` to `null` removes the parent assignment, promoting the department to top-level.

The organization_id and departmentId are resolved from path parameters and not included in the request body. On successful validation, executes: UPDATE erp_hrm_departments SET name=$1, description=$2, parent_id=$3, updated_at=now() WHERE id=departmentId AND organization_id=organizationId AND deleted_at IS NULL. Business validations: (1) name must be unique within organization (@@unique([organization_id, name])), excluding the current department id; (2) parentId if non-null must reference an existing non-deleted department in the same organization with parent_id IS NULL (top-level only); (3) parentId cannot equal departmentId (no self-reference); (4) if the department already has active children (other departments with parent_id = departmentId), parentId cannot be set to non-null, as that would create 2-level nesting depth.

IErpHrmProjectMember.description:
Represents a formal project membership assignment within the ERP HRM system. Each record links an organization member to a specific project, granting them participation rights and defining their project-scoped authority level.

The `projectRole` field determines the member's authority within the project. A `member` role grants standard contributor access — the member can log time against the project and view its tasks. A `project-lead` role additionally grants the authority to create, edit, and manage tasks within the assigned project, without requiring broader organization-level project management permissions.

This record is the prerequisite for time logging against a project and for visibility into project tasks. Each organization member can hold at most one membership per project. Soft-deleted memberships (where `deletedAt` is set) represent historical participation records and are preserved for audit purposes.

The FK column organization_member_id is resolved via JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members (with further joins to erp_hrm_members and user profile data) to produce the nested organizationMember object (IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary). deleted_at is nullable; always included in responses as null or a datetime string. The projectRole value must be one of: 'member' or 'project-lead'.

Request body for updating an existing task within a project. All fields are optional — only the fields explicitly provided will be modified; omitted fields retain their current values.

The `status` field accepts one of: `open`, `in-progress`, `completed`, `closed`. Changing the status automatically creates an immutable audit entry in the task history log.

The `priority` field accepts one of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent`.

Query erp_hrm_employee_contracts WHERE organization_member_id = :organizationMemberId. IErpHrmTimesheet.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new draft timesheet for the currently authenticated organization member.

A timesheet covers exactly one calendar week, identified by its start date (always a Monday) and end date (always the following Sunday). The authenticated member's identity is derived from the session and does not need to be supplied. Upon successful creation, the timesheet is placed in 'draft' status.

No two timesheets for the same member may cover the same week; submitting a duplicate week will result in a conflict error.

IErpHrmTimelog.IRequest.description:
Request body for the paginated timelog list endpoint (`PATCH /erpHrm/member/timelogs`). All fields are optional and combinable. Supports filtering by date range, project, task, billable status, and organization member. Pagination is controlled via `page` and `limit`.

A standard member (without `time:view_all`) may only view their own timelogs — the `memberOrganizationMemberId` filter is restricted to their own identity. A member with the `time:view_all` permission may use `memberOrganizationMemberId` to narrow results to any specific member in their organization.

This is a search/filter request DTO for the timelog list endpoint (PATCH /erpHrm/member/timelogs). It does not map to a single database table; instead, each property drives a WHERE clause filter or pagination parameter applied against erp_hrm_timelogs.

All fields are optional and combinable. Implementation steps:
1. Resolve the authenticated member's organization context from the JWT session.
2. Determine access scope: if the caller does NOT have the 'time:view_all' permission, force organization_member_id = caller's own organization_member_id regardless of memberOrganizationMemberId.
3. Apply optional WHERE filters: work_date >= startDate, work_date <= endDate, project_id = projectId, task_id = taskId, billable = billable, organization_member_id = memberOrganizationMemberId (only if privileged).
4. Validate projectId exists in organization (404 if not). Validate taskId belongs to projectId if both provided (400 if not).
5. Pagination: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit; default limit = 20. Sort: work_date DESC, created_at DESC.

IErpHrmTaskHistory.description:
A single immutable task history entry representing one status transition event on a task within the ERP HRM system.

Each TaskHistory record is automatically created by the system whenever a task's status changes. It captures the status before the transition (`oldStatus`), the status after the transition (`newStatus`), the exact timestamp of the change (`createdAt`), and the organization member who performed the change (`recorder`).

Valid values for `oldStatus` and `newStatus` are: `open`, `in_progress`, `completed`, and `closed`. These entries form a chronological, append-only audit trail for the full lifecycle of any given task.

TaskHistory records are strictly read-only — they cannot be created, modified, or deleted through the API.

The `organizationMember` relation (FK: erp_hrm_organization_member_id → erp_hrm_organization_members.id) is joined and returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary under the DTO key `recorder`. Both FK scalar columns (erp_hrm_task_id and erp_hrm_organization_member_id) are excluded from the DTO since they are exposed as rich objects. This table has no updated_at or deleted_at — records are strictly immutable and append-only.

The `organization_member_id` (owner) is resolved from the JWT session. The `id` is taken from the path parameter `timesheetId`. Week dates are immutable after creation. All timestamps are server-managed.

task_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_timelogs.task_id (nullable UUID FK referencing erp_hrm_tasks.id). Represents the total elapsed time of the work session in whole minutes. Stored as an integer to avoid floating-point precision issues when aggregating across multiple timelogs.

billable.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_timelogs.billable (Boolean). Indicates whether the recorded work session should be counted as billable to a client or against a project budget. No default is applied on update — the existing value is kept if this field is omitted.

description.description: Optional free-text description of the work performed during this session. Pass `null` to clear the existing description.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_timelogs.description (nullable String). Free-text description of the work performed during this session. Supports full-text search. Providing null explicitly clears any existing description on the timelog record.

IErpHrmTimelog.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating an existing timelog record owned by the authenticated organization member. All fields are optional — supply only the fields you wish to change. The `project_id` must reference an active project within the member's organization; archived or completed projects are not accepted. When `task_id` is provided, the referenced task must belong to the same project as the timelog. Passing `null` for `task_id` or `description` clears those fields. Excluded from this DTO: id (auto PK), organization_member_id (resolved from JWT session), timesheet_id (system-managed link), created_at/updated_at (server-managed timestamps), and all relation objects (FK scalar IDs are used in request DTOs). id.description: Unique identifier of this timelog record.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated at record creation.

organizationMember.x-autobe-specification: JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members on organization_member_id. Returns IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary representing the organization member who owns this work session.

project.x-autobe-specification: JOIN erp_hrm_projects on project_id. Returns IErpHrmProject.ISummary representing the project under which this work session was performed.

timesheetId.description: The UUID of the weekly timesheet this timelog has been grouped into, or null if the timelog has not yet been submitted in any timesheet. When non-null and the timesheet is in submitted or approved status, this timelog is locked and read-only.
timesheetId.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.timesheet_id. UUID or null. Null when the timelog has not yet been included in any timesheet. Non-null when the timelog has been grouped into a weekly timesheet submission. Clients should treat this timelog as read-only when timesheetId is non-null and the referenced timesheet status is 'submitted' or 'approved'.

workDate.description: The calendar date on which this work session was performed. Stored and returned as a UTC midnight timestamp representing the date.
workDate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.work_date (Timestamptz stored as date-only, midnight UTC). Represents the calendar date on which the work session was performed. Used for date-range filtering and weekly timesheet grouping.

durationMinutes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes (Integer). Must be a positive integer (minimum 1). Stored in minutes to avoid floating-point precision issues when summing durations across multiple timelogs.

billable.description: Whether this work session is billable to a client or project budget. When true, the session is included in billable hour reports.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.billable (Boolean). Indicates whether the work session is billable to a client or counts against the project budget. Defaults to false when not explicitly specified at creation.

description.description: Optional free-text description of the work performed during this session, or null if no description was provided.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.description (String?, nullable). Free-text description of the work performed during this session. Null when no description was provided. Supports full-text search for filtering timelogs by content.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this timelog record was created.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.created_at (Timestamptz). Timestamp when this timelog record was first created. Used for sorting and audit purposes.

IErpHrmTimelog.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a timelog record, used in paginated list responses.

Each timelog captures a discrete work session performed by an organization member on a specific date, tied to a project and optionally a task. The `durationMinutes` field stores the session length in whole minutes. The `billable` flag indicates whether the work counts against a project budget or client billing.

The `timesheetId` field is critical for rendering list views: when non-null and the referenced timesheet is in `submitted` or `approved` status, the timelog is a protected record and must be treated as read-only by the client.

The `organizationMember`, `project`, and `task` fields are pre-expanded summary objects for convenient display without additional lookups.
IErpHrmTimelog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs table. Scalar columns id, work_date, duration_minutes, billable, description, created_at, updated_at are projected directly. The FK columns organization_member_id, project_id, task_id are excluded because their corresponding belongs-to relations (organizationMember, project, task) are JOIN-expanded into ISummary objects. timesheet_id is surfaced as a raw UUID scalar (timesheetId) rather than a nested object so clients can detect locked records without an extra join to load full timesheet state. The timesheet belongs-to relation is excluded; only the scalar ID is included. Sort order is work_date DESC, created_at DESC as specified.

projectId.description: Optional filter to restrict results to timer sessions associated with a specific project. When provided, only timers linked to the given project UUID are returned.
projectId.x-autobe-specification: Optional filter parameter. When provided and non-null, adds WHERE project_id = :projectId to the erp_hrm_timers query, filtering to only timers associated with that project. Accepts a UUID string matching erp_hrm_projects.id. When null or omitted, no project filter is applied.

organizationMemberId.description: Optional filter to restrict results to timer sessions owned by a specific organization member. This field is only effective for members with the `time:view_all` permission. Members without that permission always see only their own timer, regardless of this value.
organizationMemberId.x-autobe-specification: Optional filter parameter. When provided and non-null, adds WHERE organization_member_id = :organizationMemberId to the erp_hrm_timers query. This filter is ONLY applied when the requesting member holds the time:view_all permission. For members without time:view_all, the result set is always restricted to organization_member_id = <current member id> regardless of this field's value. Accepts a UUID string matching erp_hrm_organization_members.id.

hasTask.description: Optional boolean filter to narrow results based on whether the timer is associated with a specific task. Set to `true` to include only timers linked to a task; `false` to include only project-level timers with no task; omit or set to `null` to return all timers regardless of task assignment.
hasTask.x-autobe-specification: Optional boolean filter parameter derived from the task_id column of erp_hrm_timers. When true: WHERE task_id IS NOT NULL (returns only timers tracking a specific task). When false: WHERE task_id IS NULL (returns only project-level timers without a task). When null or omitted: no filter applied, all timers are returned regardless of task assignment.

sortBy.description: Optional field name to sort the timer list by. Currently only `'started_at'` is supported. Defaults to `'started_at'` when omitted.
sortBy.x-autobe-specification: Optional sort field selector. Controls which column is used in the ORDER BY clause on erp_hrm_timers. Currently only 'started_at' is supported, corresponding to erp_hrm_timers.started_at. When null or omitted, defaults to sorting by started_at. Used together with sortOrder. Pattern constraint: ^started_at$.

sortOrder.description: Optional sort direction for the results. Use `'asc'` for oldest-first or `'desc'` for newest-first. Defaults to `'desc'` (most recently started timers first) when omitted.
sortOrder.x-autobe-specification: Optional sort direction for the ORDER BY clause. Accepts 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). When null or omitted, defaults to 'desc' (most recently started timers first). Used in conjunction with sortBy to construct ORDER BY erp_hrm_timers.started_at ASC|DESC. Pattern constraint: ^(asc|desc)$.

page.description: The 1-based page number to retrieve. Defaults to the first page when omitted. Use in combination with `limit` to navigate through large result sets.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for pagination offset calculation. Used to compute SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit on the erp_hrm_timers query. When omitted or not provided, defaults to page 1. Minimum value: 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of timer records to return in a single page. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Defaults to 20 when omitted.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of timer records to return per page. Used as the SQL LIMIT value on the erp_hrm_timers query. Minimum: 1, maximum: 100. When omitted, defaults to 20. Combined with page to calculate OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit.

IErpHrmTimer.IRequest.description: Request body for searching and paginating active timer sessions via PATCH /erpHrm/member/timers. All filter fields are optional. A member without the `time:view_all` permission will always have results restricted to their own active timer regardless of filters. A member with `time:view_all` may use `organizationMemberId` to narrow results to a specific member. Supports filtering by project, member assignment, and whether a task is linked. Pagination and sort direction are configurable.
IErpHrmTimer.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Filter and pagination DTO for PATCH /erpHrm/member/timers. Queries erp_hrm_timers joined with erp_hrm_organization_members (for organization scoping), erp_hrm_projects, and optionally erp_hrm_tasks. Authorization: members without time:view_all permission are always restricted to their own timer (organization_member_id = current member id); members with time:view_all may browse all organization timers and may use organizationMemberId to narrow to a specific member. Filters: projectId -> WHERE project_id = :projectId on erp_hrm_timers; organizationMemberId -> WHERE organization_member_id = :organizationMemberId (only when requester has time:view_all); hasTask -> true: WHERE task_id IS NOT NULL, false: WHERE task_id IS NULL, omitted/null: no filter. Sorting: sortBy='started_at' with sortOrder='asc'|'desc', default started_at DESC. Pagination: page (1-based integer, default 1) and limit (integer 1-100, default 20). Always scope to requester's current organization context.

rejection_reason.description: Mandatory written explanation provided by the reviewer when declining a timesheet. Must be a non-empty string. This reason is stored on the timesheet record and displayed to the employee so they understand what needs to be corrected before they can resubmit.
rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.rejection_reason (nullable String?). Although the DB column allows null, the rejection action requires a non-empty value — validate that the trimmed value is non-null and non-empty; return 422 if blank or null. Persisted via UPDATE erp_hrm_timesheets SET rejection_reason = (this value) WHERE id = {timesheetId}.

IErpHrmTimesheet.IReject.description: Request body for rejecting a submitted timesheet on behalf of an authorized reviewer. Contains only the mandatory written reason explaining why the timesheet is being declined. The reviewer's identity is resolved automatically from the authenticated session. Used exclusively by members holding the `time:approve` permission.
IErpHrmTimesheet.IReject.x-autobe-specification: This is the request body for the reject timesheet action (POST /erpHrm/member/timesheets/{timesheetId}/reject). It carries only the mandatory rejection_reason string. Implementation: validate that rejection_reason is non-null and non-empty after trimming whitespace (return 422 if blank or null). Then execute: UPDATE erp_hrm_timesheets SET status='rejected', rejection_reason=(this.rejection_reason), reviewer_id=(JWT member's organization_member_id), reviewed_at=NOW(), updated_at=NOW() WHERE id={timesheetId} AND status='submitted'. The acting reviewer's identity is resolved entirely from the authenticated member session JWT — no reviewer fields are present in this DTO.

id.description: Unique identifier for this invitation record.

IErpHrmInvitation.description:
Full detail representation of an invitation record in the ERP HRM system.

An invitation captures the organizational intent to onboard a prospective employee. It is directed at a specific email address and scoped to a single organization. The invitation lifecycle progresses through the following statuses: `pending` (issued and awaiting registration), `accepted` (the invitee has registered and been linked to the organization), `rejected` (declined), `expired` (validity period exceeded), or `cancelled` (revoked by an administrator or the issuing member).

The `memberId` field is `null` while the invitation is in the `pending` state and is populated with the platform-level member account ID once the invitee has registered or been matched. The `organization` and `invitingMember` fields provide embedded summary context about the organizational scope and who issued the invitation respectively.
IErpHrmInvitation.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_invitations table. Scalar columns id, email, status, created_at, updated_at are mapped directly. The FK column erp_hrm_organization_id is resolved via JOIN to erp_hrm_organizations and returned as IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary in the 'organization' field. The FK column erp_hrm_organization_member_id is resolved via JOIN to erp_hrm_organization_members and returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary in the 'invitingMember' field. The FK column erp_hrm_member_id is returned as the raw UUID in 'memberId' (nullable: null when invitation is pending, populated on acceptance). The 'member' belongs-to relation is not expanded as a nested object; only the raw UUID is exposed.

id.description: Unique identifier for this activity log entry.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated by the system when the audit entry is created.

action_type.description: Categorized label identifying the kind of business event that was recorded. One of a fixed set of recognized action types such as 'employee_invited', 'project_created', 'timesheet_approved', or 'role_assigned_or_changed'.
action_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.action_type. String drawn from a fixed set of recognized business event types: 'employee_invited', 'employee_deactivated', 'employee_reactivated', 'contract_created', 'contract_edited', 'project_created', 'project_archived', 'project_completed', 'project_deleted', 'task_status_changed', 'timesheet_submitted', 'timesheet_approved', 'timesheet_rejected', 'role_assigned_or_changed'.

target_entity_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.target_entity_type. String identifying which domain entity type the target_entity_id refers to. Possible values: 'member', 'contract', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet', 'role'.

target_entity_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.target_entity_id. UUID of the specific business entity that was affected. Used together with target_entity_type as a polymorphic reference (not a typed FK). Stored as a plain UUID.

organization_member_id.description: The UUID of the organization member who performed the logged action. Captured at the moment the event occurred and never revised, even if the member's profile changes later.
organization_member_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.organization_member_id. UUID FK referencing erp_hrm_organization_members.id. performer.description: The organization member who performed the logged action, returned as a summary object. Provides essential identity details about the actor — including their role and position — at query time.
performer.x-autobe-specification: Resolved via JOIN on erp_hrm_organization_members where id = erp_hrm_activity_logs.organization_member_id. Returns the full IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary object including the member's employment type, status, position, linked platform account, role, and department.

details.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.details (nullable String?). Optional supplementary context for the action. For example, a role change may include old and new role names; a timesheet rejection may include the rejection reason. Null when no additional context is needed.

created_at.description: The exact date and time the action was processed and this audit entry was recorded. Establishes the chronological position of the entry within the organization's audit history.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.created_at (DateTime @db.Timestamptz). Recorded by the system at the exact moment the business event is processed. This is the only timestamp column on this table; entries are immutable and have no updated_at or deleted_at.

IErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an organizational activity log entry, used in paginated list responses.

Each entry is an immutable, system-generated audit record capturing a significant business event that occurred within the organization. The entry identifies the kind of action that took place (action_type), the type and identity of the business entity that was affected (target_entity_type and target_entity_id), the organization member who performed the action (performer), and any supplementary contextual details.

Activity log entries are permanently preserved and cannot be created, modified, or deleted through any user-facing operation. The created_at timestamp records the exact moment the event was processed by the system.
IErpHrmActivityLog.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs. All scalar columns (id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, organization_member_id, details, created_at) are included directly. The performer belongs-to relation is resolved via JOIN on erp_hrm_organization_members where organization_member_id = erp_hrm_organization_members.id, and returned as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. organization_id is excluded because the organization context is determined by the authenticated member session. The organization belongs-to relation is also excluded for the same reason. No updated_at or deleted_at columns exist on this table — entries are immutable and append-only.

targetMemberId.description: The unique identifier (`erp_hrm_organization_members.id`) of the organization member who will receive the Owner role. The designated member must already be an active member of this organization and must not currently hold the Owner role.
targetMemberId.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table FK referencing erp_hrm_organization_members.id — the per-organization identity record of the member who will receive the Owner role. Not a direct column of erp_hrm_organizations. The service must: (a) look up the erp_hrm_organization_members record by this id and verify it belongs to the organizationId from the path, (b) verify status = 'active', (c) verify the member does not already hold the built-in Owner role. After validation, set this member's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to the Owner role ID and update erp_hrm_organizations.owner_member_id to this member's erp_hrm_members.id.

outgoingOwnerRoleId.description: The unique identifier (`erp_hrm_roles.id`) of the non-Owner role within this organization that the outgoing owner will be reassigned to after the transfer. Must be a valid role belonging to this organization and must not be the built-in Owner role.
outgoingOwnerRoleId.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table FK referencing erp_hrm_roles.id — the role within this organization that the outgoing owner (the caller) will be reassigned to after the transfer completes. Not a direct column of erp_hrm_organizations. The service must: (a) look up the erp_hrm_roles record by this id, (b) verify erp_hrm_roles.erp_hrm_organization_id = the organizationId from the path, (c) verify it is NOT the built-in Owner role (is_builtin = true AND name = 'Owner'). After validation, set the caller's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to this value in the transaction.

IErpHrmOrganization.ITransferOwnership.description:
Request body for transferring organization ownership from the current Owner to another active member.

The caller must be the current Owner of the organization (identified by the `organizationId` path parameter). They specify which existing active organization member should receive the Owner role (`targetMemberId`), and which non-Owner role they themselves should be demoted to after the transfer (`outgoingOwnerRoleId`).

Both fields are required. The target member must be an active member of the organization and must not already hold the Owner role. The outgoing owner role must be a valid role within the organization that is not the built-in Owner role.
IErpHrmOrganization.ITransferOwnership.x-autobe-specification:
This is the request body DTO for POST /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/ownership/transfer. It carries two FK references needed to execute the ownership transfer transaction atomically:
1. targetMemberId: the erp_hrm_organization_members.id of the member who will receive the Owner role. The service layer must verify: (a) this member belongs to the organization identified by the path parameter organizationId, (b) has status='active', (c) is not already the Owner.
2. outgoingOwnerRoleId: the erp_hrm_roles.id that the current owner (caller) will be reassigned to after the transfer. The service layer must verify: (a) this role belongs to the same organization, (b) is NOT the built-in Owner role.
Transaction steps: (a) set target member's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to the Owner role ID, (b) set caller's erp_hrm_organization_members.role_id to outgoingOwnerRoleId, (c) update erp_hrm_organizations.owner_member_id to the target member's erp_hrm_members.id (platform-level member FK), (d) set updated_at=NOW() on both erp_hrm_organization_members records and the erp_hrm_organizations record. Returns the updated IErpHrmOrganization.

IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a timesheet record, returned as items in paginated list responses.

A timesheet groups an employee's work sessions (timelogs) for a single calendar week (Monday through Sunday) and tracks the submission and approval lifecycle. The status field reflects the current state: 'draft' (not yet submitted), 'submitted' (awaiting review), 'approved' (accepted by reviewer), or 'rejected' (declined, returned to draft for revision).

The total_hours figure is computed from the sum of all associated timelog durations and is not stored directly on the timesheet record. For timesheets that have been reviewed (approved or rejected), the reviewer's identity, reviewed_at timestamp, and (if rejected) rejection_reason are included to provide a clear audit trail.
IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Fetch the timesheet row from erp_hrm_timesheets by id. Join erp_hrm_organization_members on organization_member_id to populate the owner field as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. Left-join erp_hrm_organization_members on reviewer_id to populate the reviewer field as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary (null when reviewer_id IS NULL). Compute total_hours by summing the duration values of all erp_hrm_timelogs rows WHERE timesheet_id = this timesheet's id; return 0.0 when no timelogs exist. Expose scalar columns directly: id (UUID), status (string enum: draft/submitted/approved/rejected), week_start_date (Monday, date-time), week_end_date (Sunday, date-time), submitted_at (nullable date-time), reviewed_at (nullable date-time), rejection_reason (nullable string), created_at, updated_at. Exclude raw FK columns organization_member_id and reviewer_id from the response.

IErpHrmTimer.description:
A full detail representation of an active real-time tracking timer session owned by an organization member.

A timer is a transient record that captures a live work session in progress. Each member may have at most one active timer at any given time. The timer is bound to exactly one project and optionally to one task within that project. The `started_at` timestamp marks the exact moment the session began, allowing clients to compute elapsed duration in real time.

Timer records do not have `updated_at` or `deleted_at` fields — they are permanently removed from the database when the member stops the timer (which produces a Timelog) or discards it (no Timelog created). This type is returned by timer creation, retrieval, and update operations.
IErpHrmTimer.x-autobe-specification: This DTO maps directly to the erp_hrm_timers table. Scalar fields (id, description, started_at, created_at) are direct column mappings. The three FK columns (organization_member_id, project_id, task_id) are NOT exposed as raw IDs; instead they are resolved via JOIN and returned as nested ISummary objects: organizationMember (JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members), project (JOIN erp_hrm_projects), task (LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_tasks — nullable when task_id IS NULL). No updated_at or deleted_at columns exist on erp_hrm_timers — the record is permanently deleted upon stop or discard. Elapsed duration is NOT computed server-side; clients derive it from started_at.

When omitted or empty, no status restriction is applied and timesheets of all statuses are returned (subject to the caller's access level). Multiple values may be combined.

startDate.description: Optional inclusive lower bound for the timesheet week start date filter. When provided, only timesheets whose calendar week begins on or after this date are returned. ISO 8601 date-time value representing the inclusive lower bound of the calendar week start date range. When omitted, no lower bound is applied on week_start_date.

endDate.description: Optional inclusive upper bound for the timesheet week end date filter. When provided, only timesheets whose calendar week ends on or before this date are returned. Should be an ISO 8601 date-time value, ideally aligned to a Sunday. When omitted, no upper date boundary is applied.
endDate.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.week_end_date column. Applied as: WHERE week_end_date <= endDate. ISO 8601 date-time value representing the inclusive upper bound of the calendar week end date range. When omitted, no upper bound is applied on week_end_date.

When provided by a privileged caller, only timesheets owned by that member are returned. Regular members without elevated permissions are always scoped to their own timesheets regardless of this field. When omitted by a privileged caller, timesheets from all accessible members are returned.
organizationMemberId.x-autobe-specification: Filter parameter mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets.organization_member_id column. Applied as: WHERE organization_member_id = organizationMemberId. This filter is ONLY honored when the authenticated caller holds 'time_approve' or 'time_view_all' permission. If the caller lacks these permissions, this field is silently ignored and the query is automatically scoped to the caller's own organization_member_id. When omitted by a privileged caller, all organization members' timesheets are included within their permission scope.

page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination query parameter with no direct DB column. Used to compute SQL OFFSET: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. 1-based page number; default is 1 when omitted. Minimum value is 1. Combined with the limit parameter to produce bounded, paginated result sets.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of timesheet records to return per page. Controls the page size of the paginated result. Defaults to 20 when omitted. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination query parameter with no direct DB column. Applied as the SQL LIMIT clause. Controls how many timesheet records are returned per page. Default is 20 when omitted. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100. Combined with the page parameter to produce bounded, paginated result sets.

IErpHrmTimesheet.IRequest.description: Request body for the timesheet list endpoint, providing optional filters and pagination parameters. Allows authenticated members to query their own timesheets, while members with elevated permissions (time_approve or time_view_all) can additionally filter by a specific organization member's timesheets or browse all timesheets across the organization. All fields are optional. When no filters are provided, the results are scoped by the caller's access level and returned in reverse chronological order by week start date.
IErpHrmTimesheet.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This request DTO provides optional filter and pagination parameters for querying the erp_hrm_timesheets table. Pagination: page is 1-based page number (default: 1), limit is page size (default: 20, max: 100). Sorting default: ORDER BY week_start_date DESC. All filters are optional; omitting a filter means no restriction on that dimension.

IErpHrmTimelog.description:
Complete detail record of a timelog entry representing a discrete completed work session owned by an organization member.

A timelog captures the date on which work was performed, the duration of the session in whole minutes, whether the session is billable, the project under which the work was done, and optionally the specific task the work relates to. It may also be linked to a weekly timesheet once the member submits their work hours for review.

The `locked` field indicates whether the timelog is currently immutable due to its linked timesheet having been approved. When `locked` is `true`, update and delete operations on this timelog will be rejected. The lock is lifted if the timesheet is subsequently rejected and returned to draft status.

The `owner` field provides the identity of the organization member who created and owns this timelog. The `project` and `task` fields provide lightweight summaries of the associated work context. The `timesheet` field is present when the timelog has been included in a weekly timesheet submission.
IErpHrmTimelog.x-autobe-specification: Fetch a single erp_hrm_timelogs record by id. JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members (via organization_member_id) and return as IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary for the owner field. JOIN erp_hrm_projects (via project_id) and return as IErpHrmProject.ISummary for the project field. LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_tasks (via task_id) and return as IErpHrmTask.ISummary or null for the task field. LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_timesheets (via timesheet_id) and return as IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary or null for the timesheet field. Compute locked = (timesheet != null && timesheet.status == 'approved'). All scalar columns (id, work_date, duration_minutes, billable, description, created_at, updated_at) are direct mappings from erp_hrm_timelogs.

IErpHrmTimesheet.description:
Full detail representation of a weekly timesheet record owned by an organization member.

A timesheet covers exactly one calendar week, defined by its `weekStartDate` (always a Monday) and `weekEndDate` (always the following Sunday). Timesheets progress through a review lifecycle: draft → submitted → approved or rejected. A rejected timesheet returns to draft status, allowing the employee to revise their timelogs and resubmit.

The `totalMinutes` field is computed from the sum of all associated timelog durations and is not stored directly in the database. The `reviewer` field is populated once a manager has acted on the timesheet (approved or rejected), along with the `reviewedAt` timestamp. If the timesheet was rejected, `rejectionReason` contains the mandatory explanation provided by the reviewer.
IErpHrmTimesheet.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets. owner: JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members ON organization_member_id = id → IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. reviewer: LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_organization_members ON reviewer_id = id → nullable IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary. timelogs: SELECT * FROM erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = this.id → IErpHrmTimelog.ISummary[]. total_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes) FROM erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE timesheet_id = this.id; defaults to 0 when no timelogs exist.

action_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.action_type. One of the fixed recognized values: 'employee_invited', 'employee_deactivated', 'employee_reactivated', 'contract_created', 'contract_edited', 'project_created', 'project_archived', 'project_completed', 'project_deleted', 'task_status_changed', 'timesheet_submitted', 'timesheet_approved', 'timesheet_rejected', 'role_assigned_or_changed'. import { IEntity } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IEntity";
import { IErpHrmProject } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IErpHrmProject";
import { DeepPartial } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/typings/DeepPartial";
import { ArrayUtil, RandomGenerator } from "@nestia/e2e";
import { randint } from "tstl";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

export function prepare_random_erp_hrm_project(
  input?: DeepPartial<IErpHrmProject.ICreate> | undefined,
): IErpHrmProject.ICreate {
  return {
    name: input?.name ?? RandomGenerator.name(),
    color:
      input?.color ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "#FF5733",
        "#33FF57",
        "#3357FF",
        "#FF33A8",
        "#A833FF",
        "#33FFF5",
        "#FF8C33",
        "#8CFF33",
        "#338CFF",
        "#FF3333",
      ] as const),
    description:
      input?.description !== undefined
        ? (input.description ?? null)
        : RandomGenerator.content({ paragraphs: 1 }),
    budget_hours:
      input?.budget_hours !== undefined
        ? (input.budget_hours ?? null)
        : typia.random<
            number &
              tags.Type<"double"> &
              tags.ExclusiveMinimum<0> &
              tags.Maximum<10000>
          >(),
    started_at:
      input?.started_at !== undefined
        ? (input.started_at ?? null)
        : typia.random<string & tags.Format<"date-time">>(),
    ended_at:
      input?.ended_at !== undefined
        ? (input.ended_at ?? null)
        : typia.random<string & tags.Format<"date-time">>(),
  };
}

scenario.draft:
Test that a brand-new guest visitor can successfully register and obtain a JWT session by submitting a unique device fingerprint along with their page URL and referrer.

Steps:
1. Call POST /erpHrm/auth/guest/join with a freshly generated unique fingerprint string, a valid href URI (e.g. 'https://example.com/dashboard'), and a valid referrer URI (e.g. 'https://google.com'). The ip field may be omitted (null/absent), letting the server capture the IP automatically.
2. Verify the response status is 201 (or 200 as per implementation).
3. Verify the response body conforms to IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized:
   - `id` is a valid UUID string.
   - `fingerprint` matches the fingerprint submitted in the request.
   - `created_at` is a valid ISO 8601 datetime string.
   - `token` object contains all four fields: `access` (non-empty string), `refresh` (non-empty string), `expired_at` (future ISO 8601 datetime), `refreshable_until` (future ISO 8601 datetime, later than expired_at).
4. Verify that `expired_at` is in the future relative to the current time (access token is short-lived, e.g. ~1 hour).
5. Verify that `refreshable_until` is significantly further in the future than `expired_at` (refresh token is long-lived, e.g. 7 days).

This scenario validates the primary success path: a completely new guest identity is created and a valid JWT token pair is issued, enabling the visitor to proceed with the platform's guest-level flows.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /erpHrm/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft:
Test the fingerprint deduplication behavior: when the same device fingerprint is submitted on a second visit, the system must reuse the existing guest identity record (same UUID and created_at) rather than creating a new one, while always creating a fresh session.

Steps:
1. Call POST /erpHrm/auth/guest/join with a unique fingerprint (first visit). Record the returned `id` and `created_at` from the response.
2. Call POST /erpHrm/auth/guest/join again with the SAME fingerprint (second visit), using the same or different href/referrer URLs.
3. Verify the second response is successful.
4. Verify that the `id` in the second response equals the `id` from the first response — the same guest record is reused.
5. Verify that the `created_at` in the second response equals the `created_at` from the first response — the guest record's creation timestamp is unchanged.
6. Verify that `fingerprint` in both responses matches the submitted fingerprint.
7. Verify that the second response contains a fresh `token` object with new `access` and `refresh` tokens (the new session tokens may differ from the first).
8. Verify that `expired_at` and `refreshable_until` are valid future timestamps in the second response.

This scenario validates the critical business rule that guest identity is stable across sessions: a returning visitor always maps to the same guest record, ensuring consistent anonymous identity tracking before account creation or login.

scenario.draft:
Test the primary success path for guest session token refresh.

**Setup:**
1. Call POST /erpHrm/auth/guest/join with a unique device fingerprint to obtain an initial IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized response. Capture the `token.refresh` value from this response as well as the guest identity fields: `id`, `fingerprint`, and `created_at`.

**Test steps:**
2. Call POST /erpHrm/auth/guest/refresh, submitting the captured `token.refresh` value in the request body as `{ refresh: "<token>" }`.

**Validations:**
- The response must be HTTP 200 with a valid IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized body.
- Response `id` must match the `id` from the original join response — guest identity must be preserved.
- Response `fingerprint` must match the `fingerprint` from the original join response.
- Response `created_at` must match the `created_at` from the original join response — the record is not recreated.
- Response `token` must be a non-null object containing:
  - `access`: a non-empty JWT string (different from the original access token).
  - `refresh`: a non-empty string (may or may not differ depending on rotation policy).
  - `expired_at`: a valid ISO 8601 datetime in the future.
  - `refreshable_until`: a valid ISO 8601 datetime in the future, and >= `expired_at`.
- The new `access` token must be different from the original `access` token issued at join time, confirming a fresh token was issued.

**Business rule:** A guest can renew their session using only a valid refresh token without having to re-join, preserving their anonymous identity across token expiry boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Call guest join first to obtain an initial refresh token that will be submitted to the refresh endpoint.

functions.name: test_api_guest_session_refresh_success

scenario.draft:
Test that a guest can perform consecutive token refresh operations (token rotation chain), verifying that each refresh produces a valid new token that can itself be used for a subsequent refresh.

**Setup:**
1. Call POST /erpHrm/auth/guest/join with a unique device fingerprint to obtain the initial IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized response. Capture `token.refresh` (refresh1), `id`, and `fingerprint`.

**Test steps — First refresh:**
2. Call POST /erpHrm/auth/guest/refresh with `{ refresh: refresh1 }`. Capture the response as authorized1. Capture `authorized1.token.refresh` as refresh2.

scenario.draft:
This scenario tests the primary success path of the member token refresh flow.

## Setup
1. Register a new member account via `POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join` using a unique email and password. Capture the `IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized` response, specifically the `token.refresh` field.

## Test Execution
2. Call `POST /erpHrm/auth/member/refresh` with the refresh token obtained in step 1 as the `refresh` field in the request body.

## Validations
- The response status must be 2xx (success).
- The response body must conform to `IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized`.
- The response must include a new `token.access` string (non-empty).
- The response must include a new `token.refresh` string (non-empty).
- The response must include `token.expired_at` and `token.refreshable_until` as valid ISO 8601 date-time strings.
- The `token.expired_at` must be in the future relative to the current time.
- The `token.refreshable_until` must be in the future relative to the current time.
- The `member` field in the response must reflect the same member account (matching `id` and `email` as returned from the join response).
- The newly issued `token.access` must differ from the original access token.
- The newly issued `token.refresh` must differ from the original refresh token (token rotation).
- The `member.deleted_at` must be `null` (account is active).

scenario.draft:
This scenario validates that a newly issued refresh token (obtained from a previous refresh call) can itself be used to perform another successful token refresh — confirming that token rotation works correctly across multiple sequential refresh cycles.

## Setup
1. Register a new member via `POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join`. Capture the initial `token.refresh` from the response.
2. Call `POST /erpHrm/auth/member/refresh` with the initial refresh token. Capture the new `token.refresh` from the response (this is the 'rotated' token).

## Test Execution
3. Call `POST /erpHrm/auth/member/refresh` again using the rotated refresh token from step 2.

## Validations
- The response status must be 2xx (success).
- The response body must conform to `IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized`.
- The response must include a third-generation `token.access` and `token.refresh`, both different from all previously issued tokens.
- The `token.expired_at` must be a future timestamp.
- The `token.refreshable_until` must be a future timestamp.
- The `member.id` and `member.email` in the response must still match the original registered member — the identity must remain consistent across refreshes.
- This confirms the append-only session model: each refresh creates a new session record and issues a new token pair without invalidating the member's identity.

scenario.draft:
This scenario validates multi-tenancy isolation: a member who belongs to one organization must not be able to retrieve the member list of a different organization they do not belong to. This enforces the data isolation rule that all data is strictly scoped to the session's active organization context.

**Setup steps (dependencies)**:
1. Register Member A via POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join.
2. Member A creates Organization A via POST /erpHrm/member/organizations.
3. Register Member B via POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join (different email).
4. Member B creates Organization B via POST /erpHrm/member/organizations (Member B is owner of Org B; Member B is not a member of Org A).

**Test execution — Cross-org access attempt**:
- Using Member B's authentication token (session scoped to Organization B), attempt PATCH /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationAId}/members (targeting Organization A's member list).
- The system must verify that Member B's session is NOT scoped to Organization A and reject the request.
- Expected response: 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found (the organization's existence must not be confirmed to unauthorized members, per the isolation rule).
- Verify that Organization A's members are NOT returned in any form.

**Test execution — Correct organization access**:
- Using Member A's authentication token (session scoped to Organization A), call PATCH /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationAId}/members.
- Verify response 200 OK with Member A appearing in the list.
- Confirm Member B (who only belongs to Organization B) does NOT appear in Organization A's member list.

**Business rule validated**: Section [468] — If a user's session is not scoped to the target organization, the request is rejected and the organization's existence is not confirmed or denied. All data is strictly isolated per organization.

- The error payload should communicate that the member is the sole owner and cannot leave.

- Sole owner restriction: the system prevents the last Owner from abandoning an organization, ensuring at least one owner always exists.
- The operation is atomic: if the sole-owner check fails, no membership changes occur.

- If another member is later added and ownership is transferred (POST /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/ownership/transfer), the original owner should then be able to successfully call DELETE /erpHrm/member/organizations/{organizationId}/members — but this full flow is covered in the ownership transfer scenario, not here.

This scenario tests the uniqueness constraint enforcement: the system must reject an attempt to add a user who is already an active member of the organization.

5. Register a second platform-level member account via POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join — this user provides a valid memberId for the test request.

**Target: PATCH /erpHrm/member/organizationMembers/{organizationMemberId}/contracts**

**Success path:**
- Call the endpoint with the employee's organizationMemberId using the owner's session.
- Send an empty or minimal request body (no filters) to retrieve all contracts.
- Assert response is 200 with IPageIErpHrmEmployeeContract.ISummary shape.
- Assert pagination metadata (current, limit, records, pages) is present and accurate.
- Assert that the data array contains all created contracts, ordered by start_date ascending.
- Each contract record must include: id, organizationMember (with member, role, department), pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, start_date, end_date (nullable), is_active, notes (nullable), created_at, updated_at.
- Assert that the active contract has is_active=true and the historical contract has is_active=false.

**Filtered retrieval:**
- Repeat the call with isActive=true in the request body.
- Assert only the active contract is returned (records=1).
- Repeat with isActive=false.
- Assert only historical contracts are returned.
- Repeat with payPeriod matching the active contract's pay_period.
- Assert only contracts matching that pay_period are returned.
- Repeat with sort='desc' to validate reverse chronological ordering (most recent start_date first).

**Empty result edge case:**
- If there are no contracts matching a highly specific filter (e.g., startDate.gte set far in the future), assert the response is still 200 with an empty data array and records=0 — not a 404.

scenario.draft:
Test that deleting a project is rejected when the project has one or more associated timelog records, enforcing the business rule that time tracking history must never be orphaned.

scenario.draft:
Test that a member with the `project:manage` permission can successfully retrieve a filtered and paginated list of tasks within a project they manage.

**Setup**:
1. Register a new member account via `POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join` — this member becomes the Owner of any organization they create, which grants them `project:manage` by default.

- Call `PATCH /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks` with no filter body — verify the response is `IPageIErpHrmTask.ISummary` with all created tasks returned, pagination metadata present (records ≥ 3, pages ≥ 1, current = 1).
- Call again with `statuses: ['open']` filter — verify only tasks with `status === 'open'` are returned.
- Call again with `priorities: ['urgent', 'high']` filter — verify only tasks with matching priorities are returned.
- Call again with combined filter `statuses: ['in-progress']` and `sortBy: 'priority'`, `sortOrder: 'desc'` — verify results respect both filter and sort order.
- Call with `page: 1`, `limit: 1` — verify exactly 1 task is returned and pagination reflects the correct total record count.

**Validation Points**:
- Each task summary must contain: `id`, `title`, `status`, `priority`, `estimatedHours`, `dueDate`, `parentId`, `assignee`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`.
- Pagination metadata (`current`, `limit`, `records`, `pages`) must be consistent with the data count.
- Soft-deleted tasks (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`) must never appear in the results.
- The owner (project:manage permission) can view tasks without being explicitly listed as a project member.

  - No `parent_id` (null — creating a top-level task)
- Capture the returned task `id` as `parentTaskId`.

Step B — Create the subtask referencing the parent (main assertion):
- Call `POST /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks` with:

  - `priority`: 'high'

scenario.draft:
Test that a project member can successfully retrieve full task detail from a project they belong to.

**Setup Steps:**
1. Register a new member account via POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join, obtaining a JWT session.
2. Create an organization via POST /erpHrm/member/organizations. The authenticated member automatically becomes the organization Owner with full permissions (including project:manage).
3. Create a project via POST /erpHrm/member/projects using the owner's project:manage permission. Record the projectId.
4. Assign the owner as a project member via POST /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/members with projectRole='member'. This is done so the owner is tested as a regular project member participant (not relying on project:manage bypass).
5. Create a task inside the project via POST /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks with a title, description, status='open', priority='high', estimatedHours, dueDate, and assignee_id pointing to the owner's organization member ID. Record the taskId.

**Primary Assertion (Success Path):**
- Call GET /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId} as the owner (who is also an active project member).
- Expect HTTP 200 with a complete IErpHrmTask response.
- Verify the response includes:
  - `id` matches the created taskId.
  - `title`, `description`, `status` ('open'), `priority` ('high'), `estimatedHours`, `dueDate` match what was submitted at creation.
  - `project` is a non-null summary with the correct project id and name.
  - `assignee` is a non-null IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary referencing the owner.
  - `parent` is null (top-level task).
  - `subtasks` is an empty array (no subtasks created).
  - `taskHistories` contains at least one entry representing the creation event, ordered by createdAt ASC.
  - `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are valid ISO 8601 timestamps.
  - `deletedAt` is null.

**Edge Case - Verify task history on creation:**
- The first taskHistory entry should record the initial status transition (old_status before creation, new_status = 'open') set at creation time.

This scenario validates the primary happy-path use case: a project member accessing a task's complete detail with all related entities properly resolved.

scenario.draft:
Test that task detail correctly represents the one-level subtask hierarchy: a parent task shows its subtasks list, and a subtask shows its parent reference.

**Setup Steps:**
1. Register a member via POST /erpHrm/auth/member/join and obtain a JWT session.
2. Create an organization via POST /erpHrm/member/organizations (member becomes Owner).
3. Create a project via POST /erpHrm/member/projects. Record projectId.
4. Assign the owner as a project member via POST /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/members with projectRole='project-lead' so they can create tasks.
5. Create a top-level parent task via POST /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks with title='Parent Task', status='open', priority='medium', parent_id=null. Record parentTaskId.
6. Create a subtask via POST /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks with title='Subtask', parent_id=parentTaskId. Record subtaskId.

**Assertion A - Retrieve the Parent Task:**
- Call GET /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{parentTaskId}.
- Expect HTTP 200 with an IErpHrmTask response.
- Verify `parent` is null (it is a top-level task).
- Verify `subtasks` array is non-empty and contains exactly one entry matching the subtask's id and title.
- Verify each subtask in `subtasks` is an IErpHrmTask.ISummary with the correct `parentId` set to parentTaskId.

**Assertion B - Retrieve the Subtask:**
- Call GET /erpHrm/member/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{subtaskId}.
- Expect HTTP 200 with an IErpHrmTask response.
- Verify `parent` is a non-null IErpHrmTask.ISummary referencing the parentTaskId.
- Verify `subtasks` is an empty array (subtasks cannot themselves have subtasks — only one level of nesting is supported).
- Verify `parent.id` equals parentTaskId.

**Business Rule Validation:**
- Confirms the one-level subtask hierarchy constraint is correctly represented in the API response.
- The parent task's `subtasks` array must be populated automatically by the system without any additional API calls.
- A subtask's `parent` field must reference the correct top-level task.
